History:
• 19-year-old female presents with 3-day history of burning/stinging pain on urination (dysuria).  
• Associated symptoms: single episode of visible blood in urine earlier today, foul-smelling urine, mild cramp-like suprapubic (“lower tummy”) discomfort during micturition.  
• Denies urinary frequency, urgency, flank/back pain, nausea, vomiting, fever, chills, or vaginal/urethral discharge.  
• Bowels normal; no diarrhoea.  
• Menses: last period “a couple of weeks ago” (doctor documented “three weeks ago” – conflict noted). No suspicion of pregnancy but not formally tested.  
• Sexual history: sexually active with boyfriend of 2 months; uses condoms; never had an STI screen.  
• No recent travel, new medications, or known chemical exposures.

Past Medical History:
• Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS).  
• Allergies: Clindamycin → swelling (likely angio-edema).  
• Medications: none regular. Tried OTC bicarbonate (dose/route/frequency not documented) without benefit.  
• Surgical history, hospitalisations: none reported.  
• Family history: no known renal/urinary conditions.  
• Social: College biology student; lives with friends; non-smoker; weekend social alcohol use; barrier contraception.

Physical Examination:
• Tele-visit; no in-person exam performed.  
• General appearance (via video): appears well, conversant.  
• Vitals, abdominal, CV, respiratory, GU exam: Not recorded.

Impression:
Most likely uncomplicated acute cystitis/urinary tract infection.  
Alternate considerations consistent with history:  
1. Chlamydial/gonococcal urethritis ‑ new partner, no prior screening.  
2. Distal ureteric/bladder calculus ‑ hematuria but less likely given absence of colic.  

Management Plan:
• Empiric antibiotics: Nitrofurantoin or Trimethoprim, one tablet twice daily for 3 days (exact strength/route not documented).  
• Hydration: encourage increased oral fluids; consider cranberry juice.  
• Symptom monitoring (“safety-net”): return/call if no improvement after course, or earlier if fever, flank/back pain, or feeling systemically unwell (concern for ascending infection).  
• Activity/sexual health: avoid sexual intercourse until symptoms resolve; continue condom use thereafter.  
• Consider home pregnancy test if any doubt about pregnancy status.  
• Offer STI screening at next visit due to new sexual partner and no prior testing.

Patient Summary:
Jessica Smith, 19, reports 3 days of dysuria, mild suprapubic discomfort, malodorous urine, and one episode of hematuria. Clinical picture suggests simple lower UTI; empiric 3-day antibiotic course and supportive advice provided with clear safety-net instructions.

Key Takeaways:
• Start prescribed antibiotic today and complete full 3-day course.  
• Drink plenty of water; cranberry juice optional.  
• Seek care promptly if fever, back pain, or symptoms persist/worsen.

Next Steps:
• Phone or in-person review if symptoms not improved by end of week.  
• Urinalysis/culture, STI screen, and pregnancy test to be arranged if recurrence or poor response.  

Quality checks (document_quality):
• Missing elements: vitals, physical exam findings, urine dip/culture, medication dose/strength, full obstetric/gynecologic history.  
• Conflict: timing of last menstrual period (“couple of weeks” vs physician’s “three weeks”).  
• Transcript quality: clear; minor interruptions but overall adequate for documentation.
